results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 81 outline summaries (5 callouts plus 76 units) match the controlling ideas of their aligned spec paragraphs in spec order; no unit is unmatched except the introduction callouts, which carry the thesis statement and roadmap.

Concepts ¶7 (p13), marked two_ideas: the spec's controlling idea is the pair of tactical terms the chapter needs (aggregate and domain event); the paragraph introduces them as one unit ('Two more terms come from DDD's tactical design').

One Listing ¶4 (p24), marked two_ideas: one owner and the separate property are both the 'same structure' the reference models reach; the paragraph's single idea is that independent models reach that structure because the listing is a publication about the thing.
Every unit ties to S1, S3, S4 or S5 through its section's advances_thesis; the transition and pointer units (p03, p41, p47, p54, p59a, p74, p77) serve the flow.

Each table is framed by a sentence stating its point (e.g. 'Each style fits one kind of interaction; a shared database fits none'); Figures 1-4 are followed or preceded by the claim they show; every quotation (Fowler, Vinted, AutoScout24/InfoQ, Kleinanzeigen, Adevinta 2023 and 2025, the reference model) is followed by what it shows.

results.quote: The book also draws on two generic domain models, one for a general-listings marketplace and one for a real-estate marketplace, which are the author's working models and describe no company.
results.finding: Declared similarity carrying 'the structure Veldmark's contexts show', placed at the start of p24. The opening sentence introduces a new source and picks up nothing from p21-p23; the similarity ('They reach the same structure by a different route') arrives only in the second sentence. Both flow readers stopped at this sentence.

results.quote: The context map's skeleton is shared across verticals. What changes is which contexts exist, which are core and where the entity sits.
results.finding: Declared contrast carrying 'decisions that apply to every marketplace' (the three trade-offs) into 'what differs by vertical'. The opening picks up the context map, not the trade-offs just made, so the boundary from Trade-offs is unmarked and the section's position goes unexplained (both flow readers questioned it).
All other declared transitions (introduction, section openings and paragraph boundaries) are expressed at the start of the aligned unit and pick up the declared known information.

results.quote: the other two agencies publish through two different real-estate software vendors at €389,000 and €395,000; Step 2 below explains why.
results.finding: Flow-A item 1: 'I stopped to wonder what "Step 2" meant. Its answer (prices include agency fees) comes about ninety lines later in the worked example.' The forward reference points to a numbered step three sections away; the order is fine (the worked example may explain the fee basis), but the prose should explain the difference in half a sentence here or drop the forward pointer.
results.corroborated_by: flow-B item 1 ('A forward reference to a step that does not exist yet ... I stopped and looked for a Step 1 nearby.')

results.quote: The book also draws on two generic domain models, one for a general-listings marketplace and one for a real-estate marketplace, which are the author's working models and describe no company.
results.finding: Flow-A item 2: 'I had to re-read to work out what these models were and why they appear here, in the middle of the Veldmark discussion.' The spec places the reference models here as a similarity to Veldmark's structure (decision of 2026-11-12); the prose opens on the source rather than on the shared structure, so the link is not visible.
results.corroborated_by: flow-B item 2 ('The reference models arrive without warning ... a new kind of source dropped into a section about Veldmark's contexts.')

results.quote: Even their mistakes make the case for named owners: the general model's data catalog assigns credentials, sessions and the audit log to the cookie-consent capability, a reminder that ownership assignments must be reviewed as carefully as boundaries.
results.finding: Flow-A item 3: 'I read it twice before I saw how a mis-assignment supports "named owners". It is a tangent at the end of the section.' The spec keeps the point; the prose does not say why a wrong assignment argues for named, reviewed owners in a listing system.
results.corroborated_by: flow-B item 2 (quotes the same sentence: 'I had to re-read it. The cookie-consent detail is about a model the reader has only just met, and it leads away from the listing.')

results.quote: Hearthly's events reach the group event backbone through a bridge from Google Pub/Sub.
results.finding: Flow-A item 5: 'Nothing before it prepares for this, and it means nothing until Step 4 names the bridge as one of four anti-corruption layers.' The spec puts the bridge in p28 so that p51 holds no surprise; the sentence is appended as plumbing and not tied to the paragraph's point (the same published language reaches the backbone from every brand, Hearthly's through a translating bridge).
results.corroborated_by: flow-B item 3 ('An unrelated sentence closes the paragraph on the catalog as open host service ... It makes sense only later, when Step 4 lists the bridge as an anti-corruption layer.')

results.quote: The context map's skeleton is shared across verticals.
results.finding: Flow-B, section list: 'Vertical Differences: The placement is only partly clear ... I could not tell why it belongs there rather than elsewhere.' The declared order is defensible (both readers say the current position works); the prose never states why the section follows Trade-offs, because its opening does not express the declared contrast with decisions that apply to every marketplace.
results.corroborated_by: flow-A, section 2 'Vertical Differences' bullet ('Its position is defensible, though less clearly forced than the others') and section 4 last bullet (optionally move it after Subdomains)

results.quote: In the general model, the listing is owned by one capability and read by eleven others, and two more query it through search.
results.finding: Flow-A item 4: 'The Concepts table has just said that capabilities and contexts are different units, so seeing ownership expressed per capability made me stop and check whether the word was meant.' Not reported by flow-B.

results.quote: Monetization sends `ApplyPlacement` to the catalog with the entitlement reference, and publishes `VisibilityChanged` for search.
results.finding: Flow-A item 7: 'Visibility is published before the catalog has accepted the placement (step 3), and step 4 then has to reverse it. I went back to check whether this order was intended.' The order is the spec's (p37 evidence), but one clause saying why visibility is published at once would remove the re-read. Not reported by flow-B.

results.finding: Opens from the previous chapter's capability map and the decomposition questions it leaves open, then the overloaded noun and a roadmap; none of the five weak patterns.
p76 answers the forum's question with consequences and a course of action; p77 hands off by contrast. No 'in conclusion', no new idea, no evidence that belongs in the body.

p76 joins meanings (six models) and ownership (one context decides, relationships recorded), which no single section states together, and says why it matters: the Essen Golf's removal becomes one freshness contract and brands change ranking or packages without a cross-team project.
p76 opens with the forum's question 'what is a listing, and who decides?' and answers both halves, returning to the six answers.

The cold reader predicted the sections in the roadmap's order (scene and terms, subdomains, one listing through ten contexts, context map with relationships, aggregates, listing event, Veldmark's map then the public record, then trade-offs, verticals, failure modes, Chief Architect's view, review questions), the evidence (fictional Veldmark, DDD literature, public engineering writing) and the declarative, practical tone.

The reader says the catalog decides; ingestion reads the feed removal and sends Withdraw; the catalog emits ListingRemoved on the published contract; search, alerts and leads react within declared deadlines and never write state; the delay becomes ingestion's freshness contract with the dealer. Matches the expected answer.

The reader classifies per brand (core at the private-seller classifieds brand, supporting at the dealer car brand), with a shared pipeline and policies configurable per brand and country, and the brand keeping its core contexts on a shared engine. Matches the expected answer.

The reader names separate aggregates in two contexts and Fowler's rule; describes the grant keyed by order ID, ApplyPlacement, VisibilityChanged, retries with the same key, rejection on a removed listing and monetization refunding and reversing; consistent inside aggregates, eventually consistent between. Matches the expected answer.
